Since god is largely an irrelevant concept, so I believe is the individual's position regarding his existence. Therefore, while it can be satisfying to openly and defiantly declare non-alignment with popular superstition, it doesn't serve to benefit any involved. "Believers" are likely to blind themselves to the truth and you may sacrifice the benefits of family and community based upon a relatively minor disagreement.

An inherent problem is the popular conflation of morals and piety. Many believe that the only reason not to rape and murder is that some sort of cosmic boogie-man is keeping score. Atheists, by and large, have divorced these concepts due to the necessity of living in a world without a perceived benefactor, but many theists go on in fear that Santa Claus won't leave his toys if they are bad.

Why create conflict if you can easily avoid it? Personally, I've gone to church (a bit begrudgingly, but ultimately with compliance) with my mother as an atheist because it was important to her. She felt comfort in asking for ritual protection and I wasn't so egotistical to believe that my time so important I couldn't sacrifice an hour or two. The existence of a omnipotent interloper is of equal par to the benefits of organic kale: Many have opinions, but if it's not a defining aspect of who one is, work around it through tactful silence if necessary.

If we all keep our thoughts to ourselves, to avoid unpleasantness, what about the burdens of secrecy, cheapening of relationships, and the opportunity to end the dark ages?

After the initial shock and awe, don't try to bring it up every chance you get. You're family might try to bring up religion in a nonchalant way. Just don't be enthusiastic about being atheist when they do. And remember it's your belief (or lack there of) and play it off like it's not a big deal.

Very carefully make a cost/benefit analysis.

One the one hand, you might discover the friends or relatives who are set off by atheism, which can get seriously nasty, and on the other hand, you feel a little shitty about being unable to be truthful about yourself to others.

You really can't know how far it will go until you really do announce it. Be very certain you're ready to weather that storm. Don't bother if you're easily intimidated, or going through a difficult time in other ways.
